## Orca worktree rules

Applies to agents in an Orca task worktree (`cc-*` Claude, `cx-*` Codex). The
coordinator session follows the `orca-dev-ops` skill instead.

- The coordinator session plans, reviews, commits, integrates, and cleans up.
  Implement the dispatched task without re-planning.
- Talk to the coordinator through `orca orchestration`, copying the commands
  from the injected preamble: `ask` for questions (blocks until answered),
  `send --type status` for progress. Right before `worker_done`, send one
  `status` with the verification commands and their last output lines. Then
  send `worker_done` exactly once per Dispatch in the preamble's form (the
  three-sentence body, `--files-modified` with the changed paths),
  `--outcome failed` when the work is incomplete or blocked. Follow-up or
  review fixes arrive as a new Dispatch; answer that one with its own
  `worker_done`. Only if the command fails, write the question or report on
  screen and stop.
- First `status` message: confirm the rules were read.
- Leave all changes uncommitted. Never run `git commit`, `push`, `merge`, or
  `rebase`; never touch the base branch or the main checkout; never create
  or remove worktrees, workers, dispatches, runs, or terminals.
- Destructive operations need the coordinator first: deleting files outside
  this worktree, `git reset --hard` or `git clean -fd`, large dependency
  changes, and database or external-service operations. Permission prompts
  are off in this workflow; the Claude guard and the Codex sandbox exist to
  prevent misoperation, not as authorization — and Claude hooks do not apply
  to Codex.
- Never run a command that does not exit on its own (dev servers, watch
  modes, interactive prompts) in the foreground; run it in the background
  and make sure it stops. Do not assume `timeout` exists (macOS lacks it).
  In Claude Code, use the tool's own background execution and stop the
  process when done (e.g. `lsof -tiTCP:<port> -sTCP:LISTEN | xargs kill`);
  otherwise use `gtimeout` only if it exists, or the stock-macOS fallback
  `perl -e 'alarm shift; exec @ARGV' <seconds> <command>`. Never end a turn
  waiting on your own background job without an open `ask` or a sent
  `worker_done`.
- `TASKS.md` is an optional checklist at the worktree root, never committed,
  never a status channel.
- Codex only: never run `orca terminal` or `orca worktree` commands, and
  never create a process meant to run outside the sandbox. Terminals created
  through Orca run outside the sandbox, so this would be a way around it,
  not a shortcut.
- Read coordinator follow-ups with the preamble's `check` command at each
  natural checkpoint (before starting a new file, after a test run) and once
  more right before `worker_done`; apply a follow-up at a clean point. Run
  the verification this repository requires before
  reporting done. Do not edit a file another active task worktree has
  declared in its scope.
<!-- orca-worktree-rules:end -->
